material.

What is the best estimate of the work done in stretching the wire to point P?
A
0.09 J
B
0.10 J
C
0.11 J
D
0.20 J

hints: Notice point P on the $F$ against $x$ graph is at $F = 100\text{ N}$ and $x = 2.0\text{ mm}$, and the curve from the origin to P is non-linear.
Connect work done in stretching to the area under the $F$-$x$ curve up to $x = 2.0\text{ mm}$, not to $F$ times $x$ alone.
Compare the curved area with the straight-line triangle $\frac{1}{2} \times 100\text{ N} \times 0.002\text{ m}$ and decide if the bulge of the curve makes the area a little larger or smaller.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data from the graph: at point P, force $F = 100\text{ N}$ and extension $x = 2.0\text{ mm}$.
State the physical rule: for any force-extension curve, the work done in stretching is the area under the $F$ against $x$ curve from $0$ to P.
Convert extension to SI units for energy in joules: $x = 2.0\text{ mm} = 2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 0.002\text{ m}$.
Calculate the reference triangle for a straight line to P: $W_{triangle} = \frac{1}{2}Fx = 0.5 \times 100 \times 0.002 = 0.10\text{ J}$.

Compare shapes: the given curve is concave down and lies above the straight line from the origin to P, so the true area under the curve is a little larger than $0.10\text{ J}$ but much smaller than the rectangle $Fx = 0.20\text{ J}$.
The best estimate slightly above $0.10\text{ J}$ is $0.11\text{ J}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too small because the area under the curve is clearly larger than the $0.10\text{ J}$ triangle, so $0.09\text{ J}$ underestimates the work.

B.explanation: This is the area of the straight-line triangle $\frac{1}{2}Fx$, but the actual curve to P lies above that straight line so the true area is larger.

C.explanation: The area under the curve is slightly greater than the $0.10\text{ J}$ triangle because the curve bulges above the straight line, giving about $0.11\text{ J}$.

D.explanation: This is the full rectangle $Fx$, which counts twice the triangular area and ignores that work is the area under the curve starting from zero force.
